segment.description: Obed River main stem across the Cumberland Plateau (Cumberland and Morgan counties) to the Obed-Emory confluence, within the Obed Wild & Scenic River corridor. This is the Tennessee Obed River, NOT the Obey River (Dale Hollow dam tailwater), which is catalog entry obey-river.
segment.boundaries: Headwaters in Cumberland County (USGS 03538830 at Adams Bridge sits on an upstream reach, ~20 river miles above the Emory junction per catalog) downstream to the confluence with the Emory River; TDEC scenic-river designation runs from the western edge of Catoosa WMA to the Emory confluence.

coldSource.notes: No dam tailwater: TDEC describes the Obed segment as Tennessee's only National Wild and Scenic River (designated 1976), a free-flowing main stem. Elevation is the USGS 03538830 gauge (Adams Bridge, 1365.98 ft). NRCA: Obed River 1982-1998 temperatures ranged 0.5-28.6 C with highs late June-August; continuous data at Adams Bridge Oct 2013-Sep 2016 reached ~28 C in summer.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery documented on this water (see wildPopulation), so holdover evidence was not sought or found.

wildPopulation.detail: NPS documents a warmwater fishery: 'The most common game fish caught at the Obed WSR is the Smallmouth Bass', plus muskellunge, catfish, drum, crappie, bluegill, darters - no trout on the NPS fish page. The 2017 NPS Natural Resource Condition Assessment lists 55 park fish species (Appendix G, Russ 2006 + Scott 2010a) with no Salmonidae; a string search of the full report text returns zero 'trout' hits.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: NPS documents a warmwater smallmouth-muskie river with zero trout in the park's certified fish list, and the on-river gauge hit 29.7 C on 2026-07-02.

segment.description: Clear Creek of the Obed system (Morgan County, headwaters in Cumberland County), including the Lilly Bridge gorge reach inside Obed Wild & Scenic River, to the Obed confluence near Lancing.
segment.boundaries: Headwaters (Cumberland County line) downstream to the confluence with the Obed River near Lancing; TDEC scenic-river designation covers Clear Creek from the Morgan County line to its Obed confluence; USGS 03539778 sits at Lilly Bridge near Lancing.

coldSource.notes: No dam tailwater: TDEC's Obed scenic-river designation includes Clear Creek from the Morgan County line to its Obed confluence as part of the free-flowing Wild & Scenic system. Elevation is the USGS 03539778 gauge at Lilly Bridge (1040.99 ft). NRCA: Clear Creek 1982-1998 temperatures ranged 0.3-29.2 C with highs in June-July; continuous data at Lilly Bridge Oct 2013-Sep 2016 reached 'just above 30 C (86 F) during the summer of 2016'.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery documented on this water (see wildPopulation), so holdover evidence was not sought or found.

wildPopulation.detail: NPS fish-assemblage inventories document zero trout: Russ (2006) sampled five Clear Creek locations inside Obed WSR (24 species, darters/sunfish/bass/shiners) and Scott (2010b) found 18 species including blacknose dace; the park's certified 55-species fish list (Appendix G) contains no Salmonidae, and a text search of the full NRCA report returns zero 'trout' hits. Note: the 'Clear Creek' on TWRA's trout-regulations page is a different water (Clinch River tributary, Anderson County).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: NPS surveys at five Clear Creek transects recorded zero salmonids and the Lilly Bridge gauge reached 29.0 C on 2026-07-03 (NRCA continuous record topped 30 C in summer 2016).

segment.description: Daddy's Creek (Cumberland County), gorge water in the Obed system, running its full named length to the Obed confluence near Hebbertsburg; lower reach inside Obed Wild & Scenic River.
segment.boundaries: Headwaters in Cumberland County (USGS 03539600 near Hebbertsburg at 35.9977, -84.8225) downstream to the confluence with the Obed River; TDEC scenic-river designation covers Daddy's Creek from the Morgan County line to its Obed confluence.

Elevation is the USGS 03539600 gauge near Hebbertsburg (1444.69 ft). NRCA: Daddy's Creek 1982-1998 temperatures ranged 0.3-28.4 C with the highest in July and September (mean 14.1 C).

holdover.detail: No trout fishery documented on this water (see wildPopulation), so holdover evidence was not sought or found.

wildPopulation.detail: NPS fish-assemblage inventories document zero trout: Russ (2006) sampled two Daddy's Creek locations inside Obed WSR (19 species, whitetail/telescope shiners, rock bass, smallmouth) and Scott (2010b) found 13 species; the park's certified 55-species fish list (Appendix G) contains no Salmonidae, and a text search of the full NRCA report returns zero 'trout' hits. segment.description: Clear Fork in Scott County, the wild branch of the New River system near the Big South Fork boundary, running its full named length to the New Fork/Big South Fork formation.
segment.boundaries: Headwaters near the Morgan County line (upper reach above USGS 03409500 near Robbins at 36.3883, -84.6302, drainage 272 sq mi) downstream to the confluence with the New River forming the Big South Fork of the Cumberland; HUC 05130104.

wildPopulation.detail: No fish survey or trout record located for the Scott County Clear Fork. Absence is documented only at program level: the water has no row in TWRA's 2026 trout stocking schedule and is not on TWRA's wild-trout-stream list (the TWRA live-bait 'Clear Fork' is a different water in Claiborne/Campbell counties). The NPS Big South Fork fishing page names no species and does not cover this upstream reach.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: No trout program or trout record exists for this water anywhere in TWRA/NPS sources and the on-river gauge (03409500) reached 30.2 C on 2026-08-18.

segment.description: Emory River, the Obed's downstream continuation: from its Morgan County headwaters (upper reach inside Obed Wild & Scenic River) past the Obed confluence and Nemo Bridge, through Oakdale and Harriman, to the Watts Bar embayment head where the pool carries to the Tennessee River.
segment.boundaries: Headwaters in Morgan County downstream to the Watts Bar Reservoir embayment head (Roane County); USGS 03540500 is at Oakdale (35.9831, -84.5580, drainage 764 sq mi) on the upper regulated reach; TWRA special rules run from the Hwy 27 Bridge at Harriman upstream to the Hwy 299 Bridge at Oakdale.

coldSource.notes: No dam on the Emory itself: TWRA treats the Emory as a Watts Bar Reservoir tributary (its lower end is a reservoir arm; paddlefish closure runs from the Emory mouth upstream to the Hwy 299 Bridge at Oakdale). Elevation is the USGS 03540500 gauge at Oakdale (760.98 ft). NRCA, upper Emory inside Obed WSR: 1982-1998 temperatures ranged 0.2-28.5 C with the highest in July (mean 14.1 C); 2009-2016 APHN monitoring ranged 4.4-26.1 C.

holdover.detail: No trout fishery documented on this water (see wildPopulation), so holdover evidence was not sought or found.

wildPopulation.detail: No trout documented. NPS NRCA fish inventories in the upper (park) Emory found 29 species (Russ 2006) and 34 species at five sites (Scott 2010b) with no trout; the Emory was the only OBRI watershed where muskellunge, channel catfish, and logperch were found. TWRA's Watts Bar page names the Emory a premier muskie river and lists no trout program. Segment caveat: these surveys cover the upper Emory inside Obed WSR, not the Harriman/Kingston reach.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA documents the Emory as a muskie/smallmouth river (Watts Bar arm) with no trout program, NPS park-reach surveys found zero trout, and the 1982-1998 July high reached 28.5 C.

segment.description: Brimstone Creek, a Scott County tributary of the New River in the Big South Fork subbasin of the Cumberland Plateau; no active USGS gauge and no documented access or fishery program.

segment.description: New River, Scott County, in the New River-Clear Fork system of the South Fork Cumberland basin (HUC 05130104); catalog notes it runs its full named length (Scott/Anderson counties) down to the Clear Fork confluence country. Acid-buffered plateau freestone, rain-driven flows. This is the Scott County New River, not the West Virginia New River.

segment.description: Fentress County headwaters of the Wolf River, the small riffly plateau stream that drains north into the Wolf River arm of Dale Hollow Reservoir (Obey River system, HUC 05130105). TWRA spring-stocks this reach with catchable rainbows. NOT the West Tennessee Wolf River that runs to Memphis.
segment.boundaries: Stocked reach: Fentress County headwaters (TWRA 2026 schedule row 'Fentress | Wolf River'). The USGS gauge 03416000 'WOLF RIVER NEAR BYRDSTOWN, TN' (36.560278, -85.073056) sits at the lower (Pickett County) end near the reservoir arm and is treated here as a downstream trend only, not headwater truth.

segment.description: Piney River, Rhea County, in the Spring City corridor on the Cumberland Plateau escarpment, running down to the Watts Bar embayment head (HUC 06010201). TWRA manages the reach as a Delayed Harvest trout water and spring-stocks it with catchable rainbows.

segment.description: Sequatchie Valley headwaters in Cumberland County, which TWRA spring-stocks with catchable rainbows; the river runs the full valley from the Cumberland County headwaters down toward the Tennessee River at Shellmound. segment.description: Main-stem Little Tennessee River in Tennessee below Fontana Dam (NC): the Calderwood and Chilhowee pools and the Chilhowee tailwater arm down through Tellico Reservoir to Tellico Dam. TWRA's own where-to-fish text places the trout water in 'the upper reaches of Tellico Reservoir in the Little Tennessee Arm below Chilhowee Dam' — the impounded tailwater arm, not the warm lower river or the NC river above Fontana. Owner-box note: evidence is recorded both ways below and intentionally not resolved.
segment.boundaries: From Fontana Dam (NC) down the Calderwood and Chilhowee pools to Chilhowee Dam, then the Little Tennessee Arm of Tellico Reservoir to Tellico Dam (Blount/Monroe/Loudon counties).

coldSource.notes: Brookfield Renewable operates Chilhowee Dam run-of-river (safewaters.com). TWRA's Tellico Reservoir page is direct about the mechanism: 'The upper reaches of Tellico Reservoir in the Little Tennessee Arm below Chilhowee Dam can support trout due to the cold, well-oxygenated water' released from Chilhowee Reservoir. USGS has a temperature-parameter site 03518300 (Little Tennessee River below Chilhowee Dam) but waterservices returned no temperature series for it (July 2025 IV and full-record DV queries empty), so no measured tailwater temperature is citable.

holdover.detail: Both ways, unresolved: (a) POSITIVE — TWRA's Tellico Reservoir page documents 'About 4,500 catchable Rainbow Trout are released there in the late winter and early spring annually' in the Little Tennessee Arm below Chilhowee Dam, and states the cold, well-oxygenated Chilhowee releases can support trout (agency capability statement, not creel data). (b) NEGATIVE/ABSENCE — the TWRA stocking schedule dataset snapshot (repo: packages/content/data/twra-stocking-schedule.json, 616 rows) contains no Little Tennessee River row, and TWRA's live trout page never mentions the Little Tennessee River. TWRA's year-round reservoir program list includes 'Tellico Upper (Rainbow)', which plausibly refers to this upper Tellico/Little Tennessee arm, but TWRA does not say so explicitly — identity left unresolved.

wildPopulation.detail: No wild self-sustaining population record resolved for the TN main stem; the documented fishery is the stocked Chilhowee-tailwater arm.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA documents ~4,500 rainbows planted annually in the Chilhowee-tailwater Little Tennessee Arm and states its cold, well-oxygenated releases can support trout there.

sourcesChecked: repo-local TWRA stocking schedule snapshot packages/content/data/twra-stocking-schedule.json (no Little Tennessee River row in 616 rows)

segment.description: Calderwood Reservoir, the narrow deep impoundment of the Little Tennessee River on the Tennessee/North Carolina line in Blount and Monroe counties (TWRA where-to-fish page: 541 acres, 8 miles long, described as deep with cold, clear water; bordered by GSMNP and Cherokee NF, Cheoah Reservoir upstream and Chilhowee downstream). Does not cover the Chilhowee pool below or the Little Tennessee free-river segments.
segment.boundaries: Calderwood Dam (Little Tennessee River mile ~10.5 area, near Tallassee TN) upstream to Cheoah Reservoir; most of the pool lies in Tennessee, boat access only from North Carolina per TWRA.

No measured release temperature found; release draw depth not documented in the sources checked.

TWRA's live trout page separately places Calderwood in its year-round reservoir stocking program (listed species there: Brook, Brown and Rainbow).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild self-sustaining population record resolved; TWRA describes the fishery as annually stocked (alongside bass/crappie/rock bass).

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA's live trout page lists Calderwood in its year-round reservoir trout stocking program and TWRA's reservoir page says stocked trout 'do well all year in the cold, oxygenated water'.

segment.description: Chilhowee Reservoir, impoundment of the Little Tennessee River in Blount and Monroe counties below the Chilhowee Mountains (TWRA where-to-fish page: 1,747 acres, dam completed 1957). Receives the Little Tennessee from Calderwood Reservoir upstream and discharges through Chilhowee Dam to the upper Tellico Reservoir arm. Does not cover the free-flowing Little Tennessee tailwater below the dam or Tellico Reservoir proper.
segment.boundaries: Chilhowee Dam downstream to Calderwood Dam upstream, Little Tennessee River, Blount/Monroe counties, along US 129.

coldSource.notes: Brookfield Renewable (Smoky Mountain Hydropower, ex-ALCOA Tapoco project; construction began 1955, operating 1957) operates Chilhowee Dam 'in a run-of-river mode' like Cheoah and Calderwood, following TVA Fontana Dam's peaking cycle upstream (safewaters.com facility page). The TWRA stocking schedule workbook (owner-supplied, repo data file twra-stocking-schedule.json) lists this site as type 'Winter', Rainbow Trout, stocked 1/13/2026 with next event 'TBD 12/2026'.

coldSource.notes: TWRA Statewide Trout Management Plan 2017-2027, Streams and Small Lakes section: hatchery-supported streams and lakes 'are primarily warmwater habitats that cannot support trout year round' and 'Because survival of stocked trout is usually limited by summer water temperatures, harvest of trout in these waters is generally encouraged.'

holdover.detail: No holdover evidence found for this lake. Program-level context: TWRA's plan says survival of stocked trout in these warmwater hatchery-supported lakes is usually limited by summer water temperatures and harvest is encouraged; the winter program is designed to 'provide trout angling opportunity during the winter months'. Exact 2026 dates for this site (Winter type; 1/13/2026; TBD 12/2026) come from the TWRA stocking schedule workbook (owner-supplied, no public URL).

wildPopulation.detail: No wild trout documented. TWRA's statewide plan states wild trout are generally limited to East Tennessee's mountain streams; this is a hatchery-supported put-and-take park lake in West Tennessee.
